# Glossary: modes of inquiry and terms of assessment {.unnumbered}

These are the working definitions the seminar uses. The modes of inquiry are the rows of the [inquiry-mode ledger](rubrics.qmd#inquiry-mode-ledger) and the codebook for the [corpus study](corpus-study.qmd). The terms of assessment are the variables meetings 10 to 12 measure. Meeting 1 revises this page, and the revised page is the seminar's first output, the inquiry-action vocabulary. Every definition is tied to the readings that motivate it, and every mode has three coding aids: how to recognize it in a paper, what evidence it produces, and how it characteristically fails.

Every citation links to its full record on the [bibliography](references.qmd) page, generated from `references.bib`. Nothing here is settled. A definition that fails on a paper someone in the group has written is a definition to fix, and the page records the fix.

## How to use a mode

A mode of inquiry is characterized by its epistemic function, what the work does for knowledge, and by its decisive move, the action that changes what comes next. Papers mix modes; a single study can describe, then explore, then form a hypothesis, then test it [@cleland2002]. For the ledger and the corpus study, code the *decisive* mode and record secondary modes separately. Code the mode the paper *presents*; where the trajectory is documented and differs from the presentation, record both, because the gap between them is what standing question 5 is about [@holmes1987].

Three of the rows, instruments, methods, and replication, are also contribution roles in the [Scientific Advance Profile](rubrics.qmd#scientific-advance-profile-v1). They are modes here because each has its own epistemic function: producing data that did not exist, extracting information from data that did, and testing what survives. Instruments and methods are kept apart by that line, new data against new information from existing data, and not by whether hardware is involved. Infrastructure is not a row. A seismic network, a catalog, a software package, and a standard are infrastructure for different modes, so the ledger and the corpus study record "shared infrastructure" as a flag on any row. An automated system [@king2009; @boiko2023] is not a mode of its own either: it is a method that performs some mode, and the coding question is which.

## The ten modes

| Mode | Primary epistemic function | Decisive move | Geoscience examples | Meetings |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Observation and description | Establish phenomena, baselines, distributions, and anomalies | A systematic record of what is there | Seismic catalogs, geological mapping, long-term climate records | 3, 7 |
| Exploratory discovery | Find unexpected patterns and generate questions | Looking without a stated expectation, and noticing | Unsupervised event detection, exploratory geochemistry, remote-sensing pattern discovery | 2, 6, 8 |
| Hypothesis testing | Discriminate among stated expectations or causal explanations | An observation or experiment whose outcome favors one stated explanation over the others | Testing rupture models or mantle-plume predictions | 1, 4, 9 |
| Theory and mechanistic modeling | Explain, unify, and derive consequences | A concept or formalism that reorganizes observations and yields consequences | Fault mechanics, mantle convection theory | 4 |
| Simulation and prediction | Explore counterfactuals and make conditional forecasts | Computing what a model implies under conditions not observed | Climate ensembles, tsunami and ground-motion models | 9 |
| Instruments and observing systems | Expand what can be observed | A new capability to produce data | Seismometers, distributed acoustic sensing, satellites, seismic networks | 5 |
| Methods and computation | Expand what can be inferred or calculated from observations | A new capability to extract information from existing data | Inversion methods, ambient-noise interferometry, machine-learning phase picking, community software | 5, 6, 13 |
| Synthesis and reconstruction | Integrate heterogeneous evidence into a historical or systems account | Making independent lines of evidence bear on one account | Plate tectonics, paleoclimate reconstruction, meta-analysis | 3, 10 |
| Replication and validation | Test robustness, calibration, and transferability | Repeating or transferring a result under conditions that could break it | Benchmarking models across regions; reproducing inversions | 5, 6, 13 |
| Use-inspired and co-produced research | Produce decision-relevant knowledge with users or communities | A question set with, or by, those who will use the answer | Hazard maps, climate services, Indigenous and community monitoring | none assigned |

## Coding rules

| Mode | Recognize it by | Evidence it produces | Characteristic failure | Readings |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Observation and description | A catalog, map, time series, or survey is the contribution; claims are about where, how often, and how large; no causal test | Coverage, completeness, and consistency of the record; reproducible by re-observation | Detection thresholds and coverage read as phenomena; the survey as an end in itself, Platt's "eternal surveyor" | @powell2007; @becker2019; @kuklick1996; @atwater1987; @platt1964 |
| Exploratory discovery | No hypothesis stated before the result; patterns then explanations; open-ended or unsupervised methods; a change of question mid-study | A pattern that reproduces in data not used to find it; an anomaly that explains more than the original question did | Forking paths, and a pattern found after inspection reported as a prediction; anomalies called error and dropped, which is the base rate | @steinle1997; @karaca2013; @franklin2005; @tukey1962; @bergen2019; @rouetleduc2017; @moore2025; @yaqub2018; @kuhn1962; @fugelsang2004; @ioannidis2005 |
| Hypothesis testing | Alternatives named before the outcome; a prediction that could have failed; controls, or a discriminating observable | The discriminating outcome, repeatable where the system allows manipulation; a trace that separates rivals where it does not | Auxiliary assumptions absorb the refutation; controls fixed before any data are the wrong controls; a test no outcome could fail | @platt1964; @chamberlin1965; @cleland2001; @cleland2002; @sykes1967; @bakun1985; @bakun2005; @geller1997; @schorlemmer2018 |
| Theory and mechanistic modeling | The derivation precedes the observation; a new object or concept; previously separate facts unified | Consequences later found where predicted; unification of independent evidence | A theory that predicts everything and so predicts nothing; a correct synthesis rejected on method; syntheses that, as Platt concedes, stand outside any method | @wilson1965; @vine1963; @oreskes1988; @platt1964; @cleland2002 |
| Simulation and prediction | Numerical models, ensembles, scenarios, forecasts, parameter estimation, misfit, equifinality | Skill on held-out observables; agreement across structurally different models; prospective tests | Fit mistaken for truth; simulation mistaken for experiment; validation claimed for an open system | @oreskes1994; @beven2001; @tarantola2006; @kirchner2006; @schorlemmer2018; @rainforth2024 |
| Instruments and observing systems | The sensor, platform, or network is the contribution; results framed as what can now be seen; new data | Calibration and instrument response; the same signal on an independent sensor | A feature of the measurement chain taken for a feature of the world; the researcher of one instrument | @lindsey2019; @lindsey2020; @kuhn1961; @tal2013; @platt1964 |
| Methods and computation | The algorithm, inversion, model code, or software is the contribution; results framed as what can now be computed or recovered from existing data | Synthetic tests and recovery of known signals; benchmarks against independent methods; adoption by others | A feature of the method taken for a feature of the world, such as a regularization artifact; leakage between development and test data; a loop that scores itself | @shapiro2004; @shapiro2005; @bergen2019; @kapoor2023; @langley1981; @kulkarni1988; @king2009; @boiko2023; @szymanski2023; @leeman2024 |
| Synthesis and reconstruction | No new intervention; several evidence types; a past event or a system reconstructed; reviews, meta-analyses, and connections between literatures | Convergence of independent traces; a discriminating trace, Cleland's smoking gun; a connection later confirmed by measurement | Traces attenuated or misread; false connections between literatures; retellings replacing primary sources | @cleland2001; @cleland2002; @atwater1987; @nelson1996; @satake1996; @yamaguchi1997; @swanson1986; @sourati2023 |
| Replication and validation | A known result re-obtained or moved to a new region, period, or instrument; a benchmark; a calibration study | The result survives, or fails in an informative way | Devalued as unoriginal; leakage between development and test data; a benchmark that measures the wrong construct | @lindsey2020; @nosek2018; @schorlemmer2018; @kapoor2023; @flake2020; @messick1995; @chen2025 |
| Use-inspired and co-produced research | An application partner or a decision the work informs; products such as maps, forecasts, and services; standards and guidelines as outputs | The product is used, and its use is checked against outcomes; salience, credibility, and legitimacy to the users | Usefulness mistaken for truth, or truth for usefulness; the user's question narrowing the science; use measured by citations, which miss it | @stokes1997; @cash2003; @jordan2011; @becker2019; @bornmann2008 |

### Sub-modes

The readings distinguish finer kinds of inquiry within several rows. Record the sub-mode where it is clear; it is what the ledger's "decisive move" column will often name.

- Under **exploratory discovery**: exploratory experimentation, the systematic variation of conditions without a stable hypothesis [@steinle1997]; exploratory data analysis, looking at data to find structure and questions [@tukey1962]; and serendipity, an unexpected observation recognized as worth following [@yaqub2018].
- Under **hypothesis testing**: the controlled experiment, in which the investigator produces the test condition [@cleland2002]; the discriminating observation, a test on data the system does not allow one to manipulate [@sykes1967]; and the smoking gun, a trace that picks one hypothesis out of a stated set [@cleland2001].
- Under **theory and mechanistic modeling**: conceptual synthesis, a new object that reorganizes old observations [@wilson1965]; and theory-led prediction, a derived quantity then sought [@vine1963].
- Under **instruments and observing systems**: instrument-led observation, where the questions follow the sensor [@lindsey2019].
- Under **methods and computation**: methods that create a new observable from data everyone already had, as ambient-noise interferometry did with seismic noise [@shapiro2004; @shapiro2005]; and automated discovery, a system that performs generation, selection, or execution [@langley1981; @kulkarni1988], which is coded here even when it drives a laboratory, because what it adds is the computation.
- Under **synthesis and reconstruction**: trace inference, explaining present traces by past events that cannot be rerun [@cleland2002]; and literature-based synthesis, new claims from connecting published results [@swanson1986].

## Terms of assessment

Meeting 1 fixes a first working definition for each of these, so that meetings 10 to 12 and the corpus study measure variables defined before the data are seen rather than after. Each entry gives the working definition, the measures the literature uses, and what those measures do not capture.

**Novelty.** Newness of a specific claim relative to a stated corpus and time. It is not correctness and not importance [@uzzi2013; @fontana2020]. *Measures:* atypical combinations of cited references [@uzzi2013], distance of a paper's words from the prior literature [@shibayama2021], and expert judgment, which disagrees with itself [@boudreau2016]. *Not captured:* whether the claim is true, and what the searched corpus missed. The seminar's rule is "no precedent located within this search," never "never done before." See [meeting 10](sessions/10-novelty.qmd).

**Depth.** Concentration of a researcher's or a paper's competence within one area, the opposite of breadth. *Measures:* the concentration of an author's publications across topics [@teodoridis2018; @teodoridis2019; @rassenfosse2022], and for a paper, the concentration of its references in one field, which is the low end of the interdisciplinarity measure below. *Not captured:* depth is relative to how finely a field is divided, and the same researcher is deep by one taxonomy and broad by another.

**Interdisciplinarity.** Integration of knowledge from distinct fields in one piece of work, as opposed to work that merely draws on several [@wagner2011]. *Measures:* the diversity of the fields a paper cites, counting how many fields, how evenly, and how distant they are from one another [@stirling2007; @porter2009]; the disciplines of the authors; and atypical reference pairs [@uzzi2013]. *Not captured:* field taxonomies are conventions, and a diverse reference list shows what was read, not what was understood. Where such work lands is a measured question, taken up below and in [meeting 11](sessions/11-polymathy.qmd).

**Impact.** Downstream uptake or consequence of a contribution [@dellsen2016]. *Measures:* citations normalized by field and year, which makes counts comparable across fields [@radicchi2008; @waltman2016]; models of long-term citation from early history [@wang2013]; and uptake that citations miss, such as reuse of data, software, and standards, and use in decisions, which is the whole of the use-inspired row above. *Not captured:* citations measure attention and convention as much as use [@bornmann2008], and they inflate over time [@petersen2025]. Novelty is penalized at first and rewarded late [@wang2017].

**Field-shaping.** A contribution after which a field's questions, methods, or reference set are different. Unlike novelty, it is retrospective: it is a fact about what the field did next. *Measures:* the disruption index, which asks whether later papers cite a work instead of its predecessors or together with them [@funk2017; @wu2019], with the corrections its critics require [@petersen2025; @park2023]; becoming canonical in a field that keeps citing it [@chu2021]; delayed recognition, the sleeping beauty [@ke2015]; and the appearance of a new topic whose papers cite it. *Not captured:* each measure operationalizes something different, and the seminar reports a profile rather than a score. See [meeting 12](sessions/12-scientific-advance.qmd), whose working definitions of advance, innovation, and impact this entry defers to.

**Hypothesis gate.** A rule that the next action in an inquiry must be a test of a stated hypothesis. The ledger asks, for each reconstructed episode, whether such a rule would have helped, hurt, or not applied at the decisive move. It is the design choice the seminar is questioning, and its best defenders are in the reading [@platt1964; @ioannidis2005; @king2009].

**Decisive move.** The action in an episode that changed what came next: a record, a pattern, a test, a concept, a computation, a capability, a convergence, a replication, or a question posed by a user. It is what the ledger codes, and it is inferred from the record, so its evidence basis is recorded beside it.

**Trajectory and narrative.** The trajectory is what was done, in order. The narrative is the published account. They differ [@holmes1987], and the difference is not misconduct; but only the trajectory is evidence about how inquiry proceeds, and most of what the seminar reads is narrative. Every ledger row says which it rests on.

## Where interdisciplinary work lands

The measured answer so far, which the seminar tests against its own cases. Papers that combine an unusual pairing of references with a conventional core are cited more than either alone [@uzzi2013]. Researchers who work across fields publish less and are cited more [@leahey2017]. Generalists outperform specialists where a field is moving fast and underperform them where it is slow [@teodoridis2019]. Specialization is rewarded persistently in at least one large field [@rassenfosse2022]. And the tools that lower the cost of breadth have so far narrowed what fields ask, while widening what individuals produce [@hao2026; @doshi2024]. None of this observed this group, and the [corpus study](corpus-study.qmd) is where the group would find out whether it holds in its own literature.

## Revising this page

Meeting 1's output is this page as amended. Propose a change by editing the page and saying, in the pull request, which paper the old definition failed on. Definitions of the terms of assessment are revisited in meetings 10 to 12, once the measures have been read. The use-inspired row has no assigned reading in the thirteen meetings; the three listed for it are a start, and a fourth from this group's own hazard work would be better.
